title: The Landfall of the Upper Fly River
premise: Rafael Okafor, a salvage diver haunted by a debt to the family of a drowned friend, is hired to recover equipment from a wreck in the Fly River delta that the navy officially denies exists. When a scientific expedition probing the river's forbidden upper reaches goes silent, Rafael is conscripted as their only reachable contact and sent upstream after them. He discovers the expedition found an uncharted sinkhole system feeding the river — and that the navy intends to seal it, burying evidence of a wartime atrocity along with two surviving scientists. Choosing truth over the loyalty he owes his dead friend's memory, Rafael leads them out through flooded caverns, loses the compass that anchored him to his past, and finally surfaces into daylight, free of both debt and silence.
about_author: Quentin Thornbury is the pen name of a former merchant marine officer who spent six years running cargo on Papua New Guinea's river systems before turning to fiction. His novels blend hard-won technical detail with a deep fascination for the secrets rivers keep.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wires
chapters.summary: Rafael dives a rusting freighter in the delta, recovering a sealed navy crate he was paid not to open. POV: Rafael. The beat is restless competence masking grief — we learn he owes the Okonkwo family money from a dive that killed his best friend, and that this job is supposed to settle it.

chapters.title: The Frequency That Answers
chapters.summary: A navy liaison, Commander Voss, hires Rafael to raise radio relays upriver after an expedition stops transmitting. Rafael recognizes the expedition leader's voice on a garbled recording: Dr. Amara Sesay, someone from his past. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: duty offered as escape, suspicion simmering beneath.

chapters.title: Kiwai Landing
chapters.summary: Rafael travels upriver by boat with a taciturn guide, Old Tamu, past villages that go quiet when the expedition is mentioned. He finds the expedition's abandoned first camp, ransacked but not robbed. POV: Rafael. Beat: dread builds; belonging feels like something these waters refuse to grant anyone.

chapters.title: What the Sinkhole Keeps
chapters.summary: Rafael locates the second camp at the edge of a vast sinkhole lake and finds Dr. Sesay alive, hiding with geologist Peter Anand. She reveals the team found a submerged cave network containing a sunken WWII munitions barge — and mass graves. POV: Amara. Beat: horror and resolve; the wreck Rafael was diving was its supply ship.

chapters.title: The Debt We Dive For
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present action: the dive that killed Rafael's friend Ekon, and why Rafael carries Ekon's compass. In the present, Voss's patrol boat appears downstream, hunting them. POV: Rafael. Beat: guilt crystallizes into understanding — loyalty to the dead cannot mean lying for them forever.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts Voss, who offers him money, the debt erased, and safe passage if he hands over Amara's evidence and forgets the graves. POV: alternating Rafael and Voss. Beat: temptation laid bare; love against duty sharpens as Rafael realizes what he feels for Amara is becoming real.

chapters.title: Upstream of Every Map
chapters.summary: Refusing the deal, Rafael, Amara, Anand, and Tamu flee deeper into the sinkhole system, navigating flooded galleries toward a rumored outlet. A collapse separates Anand from the group. POV: Amara. Beat: terror and trust — she must rely entirely on Rafael's diving skill in black water.

chapters.title: Black Water
chapters.summary: A near-drowning sequence: Rafael guides Amara through a submerged sump on a single line, sharing air when her regulator fails. They surface inside a cathedral cavern where Anand waits, injured but alive. POV: Rafael. Beat: intimacy forged in extremis; the compass cracks against the rock and keeps working anyway.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Climax: Voss's men flood the lower galleries to seal the caves. Rafael triggers a controlled blowout through the outlet spring, surfacing all four survivors in front of Amara's pre-arranged press contacts and village witnesses as the sinkhole collapses behind them. POV: Rafael. Beat: sacrifice of secrecy; truth wins at cost of everything hidden.

chapters.title: The Compass Point North
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the inquiry vindicates the dead expedition members. Rafael visits Ekon's family, tells them the whole truth, and learns the debt was forgiven long ago — it was only ever his to carry. He gives the cracked compass to Tamu and stays in the delta with Amara. POV: Rafael. Beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
